# What cannot be proved in the default suite, and what each entry needs instead.
#
# The default suite is pure: no display server, no elevated rights, no host font
# directory, no network. A few things cannot be proved under that rule at all,
# and letting one of them into the default run is how the pure suite gets
# quietly polluted - it passes on the machine it was written on and turns into a
# mystery for the first contributor without whatever it silently wanted.
#
# They live here instead. `.github/scripts/needs-an-environment.sh` runs them and
# holds no entry of its own, so adding one is writing a record here and a leg in
# the proof beside it. `.github/scripts/check-needs-an-environment.sh` refuses a
# record this file cannot be read from, and `docs/needs-an-environment.md` argues
# the rule and says what the checker cannot judge.
#
# One record per entry, separated by a blank line. Four fields, all required:
#
#   Id       the name the runner is invoked with, and the name a result carries
#   Needs    the environment this entry requires, in the terms somebody
#            reproducing it has to satisfy
#   Because  why it cannot be proved in the pure suite, in one sentence
#   Run      the command, from the repository root
#
# A record with no `Id` or no `Run` stops the run, because an entry the runner
# cannot name or cannot execute is not an entry. A record with no `Needs` or no
# `Because` is refused, because those two are the whole reason this file exists:
# an entry nobody can reproduce and an entry nobody can argue with are the two
# ways a harness like this becomes a place things are hidden.

Id: sealed-suite
Needs: a container runtime the calling account can drive without elevation, and, on a first run only, a network route for the single fetch of the image that .github/scripts/run-sealed.sh pins by digest
Because: the claim is about what the default suite does NOT need, and no test can assert that a display, a network route, host fonts or elevated rights are absent from the machine that is running it.
Run: bash .github/scripts/run-sealed.sh suite

Id: sealed-probes
Needs: the same container runtime, and the sealed environment the entry above builds, which is an image carrying no font file and started with no network route and a read-only filesystem
Because: a sealed environment that is not actually sealed passes the same suite, so the environment needs a proof of its own, and a probe written to read the environment is the one test that must not be pure.
Run: bash .github/scripts/run-sealed.sh probes
